Handbook: California Driver's Handbook (California DMV, United States)
Units: US customary (ft, mi, mph)
Topic: passing
Batch: the 37 selected passages from the page "Section 6: Navigating the Roads".

[p1] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Single Solid Yellow Line · ¶1 | para
A single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic. Do not pass a vehicle in front of you if there is only one lane of traffic going your direction and a solid yellow line on your side of the road.

[p2] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Double Solid Yellow Lines · ¶1 | para
Do not pass over double solid yellow lines. Stay to the right of these lines unless you are:

[p3] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Double Solid Yellow Lines · item 1 | item
In a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) carpool lane that has a designated entrance on the left.

[p4] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Double Solid Yellow Lines · item 2 | item
Instructed by construction or other signs to drive on the other side of the road because your side is closed or blocked.

[p5] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Double Solid Yellow Lines · item 3 | item
Turning left across a single set of double yellow lines to enter or exit a driveway or private road or make a U-turn.

[p6] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Broken Yellow Line · ¶1 | para
A broken yellow line indicates you may pass if the broken line is next to your driving lane. Only pass when it is safe.

[p7] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Lane Markings › Double Solid White Lines · ¶1 | para
Double solid white lines indicate a lane barrier between a regular use and a preferential use lane, such as a carpool (HOV) lane. You may also see double solid white lines in or near freeway on and off ramps. Never change lanes over double solid white lines. Wait until you see a single broken white line.

[p8] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Choosing a Lane · ¶3 | para
Here are some tips for choosing a lane:

[p9] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Choosing a Lane · item 1 | item
Use the left lane to pass or turn left.

[p10] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Passing Lanes · ¶1 | para
On a multilane road, the passing lane (far left lane) is the lane closest to the center divider and is used to pass other vehicles.

[p11] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Center Left Turn Lanes · ¶1 | para
A center left turn lane is located in the middle of a two-way street. It is marked on both sides by two painted lines. The inner line is broken and the outer line is solid. Use the center left turn lane to prepare for and make a left turn or U-turn. It is not a regular traffic lane or passing lane. You may only drive for 200 feet in the center left turn lane. To turn left from this lane:

[p12] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Turnout Areas or Lanes · ¶1 | para
Some two-lane roads have special turnout areas or lanes. Merge into these areas or lanes to allow cars behind you to pass.

[p13] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Turnout Areas or Lanes · image | figure
Figure: Alt text: “Slower Traffic Use Turnouts”

[p14] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Turnout Areas or Lanes · ¶2 | para
You must use a turnout area or lane to let other vehicles pass when you are driving slowly on a two-lane road, where passing is unsafe, and there are five or more vehicles following you.

[p15] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Bicycle Lanes · image | figure
Figure: Alt text: “Bicycle Lane”

[p16] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Traffic Lanes › Types of Lanes › Bicycle Lanes · ¶2 | para
Example of shared roadway. Three (3) feet of distance must be maintained between the car and cyclist.

[p17] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · ¶1 | para
You must judge whether you have enough space to pass whenever you approach:

[p18] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · item 1 | item
An oncoming vehicle or bicyclist.

[p19] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · item 2 | item
A hill, curve, intersection, or road obstruction. To safely pass, the hill or curve should be at least one-third of a mile ahead.

[p20] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · ¶2 | para
Before you pass, look ahead for road conditions that may cause other vehicles to move into your lane.

[p21] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · ¶3 | para
Do not pass:

[p22] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · item 3 | item
If you are approaching a hill or curve and cannot see if other traffic is approaching. This is very dangerous on one and two lane roads.

[p23] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · item 4 | item
Within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, railroad crossing, or other hazardous area.

[p24] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · item 5 | item
At crossroads and driveways.

[p25] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing · item 6 | item
Unless you have enough space to return to your lane.

[p26] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · ¶1 | para
When you are going to pass on an open highway:

[p27] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 1 | item
Signal that you plan on passing.

[p28] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 2 | item
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.

[p29] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 3 | item
Drive into the passing lane.

[p30] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 4 | item
Speed up to pass the vehicle.

[p31] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 5 | item
Signal and return to your original lane.

[p32] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · ¶2 | para
You may pass on the right only when:

[p33] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 6 | item
An open highway has two or more lanes going in your direction.

[p34] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 7 | item
The driver ahead of you is turning left and you can safely pass on the right. Never pass on the left if the driver is signaling a left turn.

[p35] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · item 8 | item
You are on a one-way street.

[p36] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › How to Pass · ¶3 | para
Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.

[p37] page: Section 6: Navigating the Roads | heading: Passing › Being Passed · ¶1 | para
If a vehicle is passing you or signals that they plan on passing, allow the vehicle to pass. Maintain your lane position and your speed.

sources.quote: Here are some tips for choosing a lane:
Use the left lane to pass or turn left.

flags.note: The handbook calls the lane for passing "the left lane" here and "the passing lane (far left lane)" under Passing Lanes (3.2.1a).

statements.note: The lead calls these items "tips", so the item stays advice. The condition comes from the heading "Choosing a Lane" and its lead.

statements.text: a driver MUST judge whether there is [?enough] space to pass WHEN approaching an oncoming vehicle or bicyclist

sources.quote: You must judge whether you have enough space to pass whenever you approach:
An oncoming vehicle or bicyclist.

flags.note: No measure of space given.
"Must" governs a mental judgment that no one can observe; the sentence may be strong advice rather than a legal duty.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle WHEN on an open highway

sources.quote: When you are going to pass on an open highway:

flags.note: On an open highway with one lane each way the lane the driver passes in is the oncoming lane, but the handbook defines "the passing lane" as the far-left lane of a multilane road (3.2.1a).

statements.note: The steps are a bulleted, unnumbered list; they are written as one PROCEDURE because the lead introduces them as what to do when going to pass and the items run in sequence.

speed up to pass the vehicle

If you are approaching a hill or curve and cannot see if other traffic is approaching. This is very dangerous on one and two lane roads.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT use a center left turn lane for passing

sources.quote: Use the center left turn lane to prepare for and make a left turn or U-turn. It is not a regular traffic lane or passing lane.

flags.span: It is not a regular traffic lane or passing lane
flags.note: The ban is implied by a description of what the lane is not; the text gives no instruction about passing.

statements.note: "You may only drive for 200 feet in the center left turn lane" limits any use of the lane and is not about passing, so it gives no statement here.

statements.text: FACT a single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic

sources.quote: A single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle in front WHEN there is only one lane of traffic going in the driver's direction AND there is a solid yellow line on the driver's side of the road

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle in front of you if there is only one lane of traffic going your direction and a solid yellow line on your side of the road.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT [?pass over] double solid yellow lines AND SHOULD stay to the right of them UNLESS the driver is in a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) carpool lane that has a designated entrance on the left OR construction or other signs instruct the driver to drive on the other side of the road because the driver's side is closed or blocked OR the driver is turning left across a single set of double yellow lines to enter or exit a driveway or private road or to make a U-turn

sources.quote: Do not pass over double solid yellow lines. Stay to the right of these lines unless you are:
In a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) carpool lane that has a designated entrance on the left.
Instructed by construction or other signs to drive on the other side of the road because your side is closed or blocked.
Turning left across a single set of double yellow lines to enter or exit a driveway or private road or make a U-turn.

flags.note: "Pass over" means driving across the lines: the rule bans crossing them, which rules out passing in the opposite lane, but it does not mention passing as such.

statements.note: The three items are exceptions to one rule, so they form one UNLESS clause rather than one statement each.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass WHEN a broken yellow line is next to the driver's lane ONLY IF it is [?safe]

sources.quote: A broken yellow line indicates you may pass if the broken line is next to your driving lane. Only pass when it is safe.

flags.note: Judgment term.

statements.note: "Only pass when it is safe" is a bare imperative that limits the permission in the sentence before, so it becomes the ONLY IF clause rather than a rule of its own.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN the driver is at a crossroad or driveway

sources.quote: Do not pass:
At crossroads and driveways.

statements.text: DEFINE the passing lane IS the far-left lane of a multilane road THAT is closest to the center divider AND is used to pass other vehicles

sources.quote: On a multilane road, the passing lane (far left lane) is the lane closest to the center divider and is used to pass other vehicles.

statements.note: Here "the passing lane" is the far-left lane of any multilane road, not an added lane as in the Ontario passing and climbing lanes.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass on the right ONLY IF an open highway has 2 or more lanes going in the driver's direction OR (the driver ahead is turning left AND the driver can pass on the right [?safely]) OR the driver is on a one-way street

sources.quote: You may pass on the right only when:
An open highway has two or more lanes going in your direction.
The driver ahead of you is turning left and you can safely pass on the right.
You are on a one-way street.

flags.note: Presupposes that passing on the right is otherwise not allowed; that default is not stated.
Judgment term.

statements.note: The three items are alternative conditions of one permission, so they are joined with OR in one ONLY IF clause; one statement per item would give three conflicting ONLY IF conditions.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass the driver ahead on the left WHEN the driver ahead is signaling a left turn

sources.quote: Never pass on the left if the driver is signaling a left turn.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass

sources.quote: Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.

statements.note: Filed under the shoulder (3.2.4): the handbook does not name the shoulder, but leaving the paved or main-traveled part of the road covers it.

statements.text: FACT some two-lane roads have special turnout areas or lanes

sources.quote: Some two-lane roads have special turnout areas or lanes.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD merge into a turnout area or lane to allow the vehicles behind to pass WHEN on a two-lane road that has turnout areas or lanes

sources.quote: Merge into these areas or lanes to allow cars behind you to pass.
Slower Traffic Use Turnouts

flags.span: five or more vehicles following you
flags.note: The next paragraph makes using a turnout a legal duty, but only when the driver is driving slowly, passing is unsafe and five or more vehicles follow (3.2.5c).

statements.note: The sign beside the paragraph reads SLOWER TRAFFIC USE TURNOUTS; it illustrates this rule and has no text of its own.

statements.text: a driver MUST use a turnout area or lane to let other vehicles pass WHEN the driver is driving [?slowly] on a two-lane road where passing is [?unsafe] AND 5 or more vehicles are following the driver

sources.quote: You must use a turnout area or lane to let other vehicles pass when you are driving slowly on a two-lane road, where passing is unsafe, and there are five or more vehicles following you.

flags.note: No speed given; slow compared with the traffic behind.
Judgment term; the text does not say who judges that passing is unsafe.

statements.note: A California-only duty of the driver being passed.

statements.text: a driver MUST keep [?3 ft of distance] between the vehicle and a cyclist WHEN the driver and the cyclist share a roadway

sources.quote: Example of shared roadway. Three (3) feet of distance must be maintained between the car and cyclist.
Bicycle Lane

flags.note: A distance without a direction: the caption does not say whether it is the side gap when passing, as the picture shows, or any gap between car and cyclist.

Passing a Bicyclist (3.4.4h) and Choose Between Hazards (3.4.4o) give at least 3 ft as advice when passing; this caption says 3 ft "must be maintained", without "at least" and without mentioning passing.

statements.note: The rule is a caption, a separate paragraph under an image whose alt text says only "Bicycle Lane". The image shows a shared lane (sharrow marking), a car behind a cyclist, and "3 FEET" marked beside the cyclist: the side gap as the car goes past.

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD allow the vehicle to pass AND SHOULD keep the lane position and speed WHEN a vehicle is passing the driver OR a vehicle signals that it plans to pass

sources.quote: If a vehicle is passing you or signals that they plan on passing, allow the vehicle to pass. Maintain your lane position and your speed.
